learning_outcomes.text: Know the planning, design, and execution process of an industrial activity.
Identify the agents, know the content, and the initial data necessary for a building execution project.
Approach and introduction to urban planning.
Classify and identify the different types of industrial building arrangements.
Classify different types of terrain and identify the predominant parameters of a geotechnical study.
Classify, determine, and identify the different types of ground conditioning.
Classify, determine, and identify the different types of foundations.
Classify, determine, and identify the different types of load-bearing structures.
Classify, determine, and identify the different types of horizontal structures.
Classify, determine, and identify the different types of envelope systems.
Classify, determine, and identify the different types of compartmentalization systems.
Classify, determine, and identify the different types of finishing systems.
Classify, determine, and identify the different types of conditioning and installations.
Classify, determine, and identify the different types of equipment.
Know how to address compliance with the Technical Building Code.
Identify the elements belonging to any of the systems described in the visited building, as well as their relationship with the constructive process and installation integration.

syllabus_topics: Conditioning and installation systems, and equipment.
Compliance with the Technical Building Code. "In situ" knowledge of building execution.
teaching_methods: Cooperative learning: Develop active learning through cooperative work strategies among students and fostering shared responsibility to achieve group goals.
Project-based learning: Carrying out a project to solve a problem, applying acquired knowledge and fostering skills related to planning, design, activity execution, and conclusion drawing.
Case study: Acquisition of learning through the analysis of real or simulated cases, in order to interpret and solve them, training various alternative solution procedures.
Exposition/Lecture: Transmit knowledge and activate cognitive processes in the student, involving their participation.
Exercise and problem solving: Practice, rehearse, and apply prior knowledge by repeating routines.

assessment_methods.method: Project (group common part and individual part, project memory with photos, and in-class presentation)

assessment_rules: The overall grade is composed of a project, which includes a group common part and an individual part (a project memory illustrated with photographs and an in-class presentation), accounting for 90%, and a computer practice for 10%. Graphic justification of attendance to building visits is required. Students must bring a PDF copy of their work for the professor and a USB drive with the project and presentation slides for the exposition. Presentations are strictly timed to 20 minutes, with 5 minutes for setup. Grading criteria value content quality in reference to the course topics and student effort relative to project difficulty.
